description: Wire per-issue workflow-profile overrides (template / variables / prompts) into the CLI via `mo issue workflow config {get,set,clear,preview}`, plus the server-side variable null-clear semantics the CLI clear verb relies on.

tasks.title: Server: variable null-clear semantics in VariableBundle.Patch/DeepMerge
tasks.spec: specs/issue-workflow-profile/spec.md#Workflow profile variable clear via null on PATCH
tasks.description: Make `PATCH /workflow-profile/variables` treat an overlay value of JSON null as explicit key removal rather than a no-op. Today `VariableBundle.DeepMerge`/`MergeNode` `continue` past null properties, so `{ "foo": null }` leaves `foo` untouched. Change the merge so an overlay null removes the key from the merged result (top-level vars and nested stage vars), while an omitted key still preserves the base value. Cover both `VariableBundle.Patch` (issue + run + project profile managers) and the stage-var merge path.
acceptanceCriteria: `VariableBundle.Patch(base, { Vars: { "foo": null } })` yields a bundle whose Vars object does NOT contain `foo`.
An overlay that omits a key still preserves that key from base (merge remains additive for present values).
Nested stage vars honor the same null-removal: `Patch` with `Stages["plan"].Vars = { "baz": null }` removes `baz` from that stage only.
`ResolveStageVars` still resolves correctly after a null-clear (no crash, removed key absent).

Unit tests in `Mohist.Server.Tests` cover: null removes top-level key, null removes nested stage key, omitted key preserved, null on a previously-absent key is a no-op, deep-merge of present values still overrides.
No existing `IssueWorkflowProfileApiSpecs` / variable-merge regression test breaks; `dotnet build Mohist.sln` is clean (TreatWarningsAsErrors).
tasks.notes: DeepMerge is shared by issue/run/project profile managers and ResolveStageVars — verify none rely on the current null=no-op behavior (audit callers; no client sends null today, so the change is backward-compatible). This is the only server change in the change-set.

tasks.title: CLI: config command group skeleton + get + preview (read path)
tasks.spec: specs/cli-interface/spec.md#CLI provides mo issue workflow config command group
tasks.description: Add the `config` subcommand group under `mo issue workflow` (in `BuildWorkflow`, `MohistCliCommands.Issue.cs`) with shared `number` arg, `ProjectRefOption()`, and `OutputOption()`. Implement the two read verbs: `config get <num>` → `GET /workflow-profile` rendered as template/variables/prompts sections, and `config preview <num> <key>` → `POST /workflow-profile/prompts/{key}/preview`. Establish the group scaffolding (the `Command("config")` parent, `-o table|json` plumbing) that T-003/T-004 attach their verbs to. Add a `WorkflowProfile` table shape for the three-section `get` response.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo issue workflow config --help` lists exactly `get`, `set`, `clear`, `preview` (set/clear may be not-yet-implemented stubs that error, but must appear).
`config get <num> -o table` sends `GET /api/projects/:pid/issues/:n/workflow-profile` and renders template, variables, and prompts sections; `-o json` emits the raw payload.
`config preview <num> plan_prompt` sends `POST /api/projects/:pid/issues/:n/workflow-profile/prompts/plan_prompt/preview` and prints the rendered prompt text.
Both verbs accept `--project`/`--project-id` and `-o table|json`; an invalid `-o` value prints a clear error and exits 1.

CLI integration tests (RecordingHttpHandler + FakeFileSystem harness, e.g. `CliIssueWorkflowConfigSpecs.cs`) assert the request method/path for `get` and `preview`, and that a non-success response surfaces the server error and exits non-zero.
tasks.notes: Reuse `PrintWithOutputAsync` for GET and `PrintPostWithOutputAsync` for the preview POST. Keep `set`/`clear` as listing-only stubs so `--help` satisfies the spec now; their full implementation is T-003/T-004. Do NOT depend on T-001 — the read path needs no server change.

tasks.title: CLI: config set (composite template/variable/prompt writes)
tasks.spec: specs/cli-interface/spec.md#CLI issue workflow config set composes template, variable, and prompt changes
tasks.description: Implement the full `config set <num> [flags]` composite write verb on the group created in T-002. Wire `--template <yaml|@file>` → PUT template, `--var k=v` / `--stage-var stage.k=v` (repeatable, merged into one PATCH variables body), and `--prompt key=body|@file` (repeatable, one PUT per key). Only categories whose flags are present fire requests; absent flags are untouched. Add `@file` reading via the injectable `IFileSystem` (strip leading `@`, `ReadAllTextAsync`) and `k=v`/`stage.k=v` parsing (split on first `=`, then first `.` for stage). Add `PrintPutWithOutputAsync` to `MohistCliApi` so the template PUT honors `-o`.
acceptanceCriteria: `config set <num> --template @wf.yaml` reads `wf.yaml` via `IFileSystem` and sends `PUT /workflow-profile/template` with the file body; a follow-up `config get` reflects it.

`config set <num> --var foo=bar --stage-var plan.baz=qux` sends a single `PATCH /workflow-profile/variables` whose body contains top-level `foo=bar` and nested `plan.baz=qux`, and sends NO template or prompts request.
`config set <num> --prompt greeting="You are..."` sends `PUT /workflow-profile/prompts/greeting` with the inline body; `--prompt greeting=@prompts/greeting.md` reads the file and sends its contents.
A composite invocation (`--template`, `--var`, `--prompt` together) issues all three requests independently.
`config set <num>` with no flags makes no HTTP request, prints a clear message, and exits non-zero.
Malformed `--var` (no `=`) or `--stage-var` (no `.`) prints a clear error and exits non-zero before any request.
A server rejection (e.g. invalid template YAML) is surfaced faithfully with a non-zero exit (spec: #CLI workflow config surfaces server errors faithfully).
CLI integration tests assert the emitted method/path/body for each flag combination and the no-op + error paths.
tasks.notes: Do NOT couple `@file` reading to `BodyInputResolver` (its error messages are issue-body-specific and its mutually-exclusive-source semantics don't fit optional repeatable flags). Prompt keys are URL-escaped (`Uri.EscapeDataString`); reject keys containing `/`. Variables default to PATCH (merge) semantics, not PUT-replace — do not add a replace mode in this task.

tasks.title: CLI: config clear (composite template/variable/prompt removals)
tasks.spec: specs/cli-interface/spec.md#CLI issue workflow config clear composes template, variable, and prompt removals
tasks.description: Implement the `config clear <num> [flags]` composite removal verb on the group from T-002. Wire `--template` → DELETE template (issue falls back to project/system template), `--prompt key` → DELETE prompt, and `--var k` (repeatable) → a single `PATCH /workflow-profile/variables` with `{ k: null }` for each named key, which removes them thanks to the server null-clear behavior from T-001. Only flagged categories are affected; absent flags leave other variables/prompts intact.
acceptanceCriteria: `config clear <num> --template` sends `DELETE /workflow-profile/template`; the issue's effective template falls back to the inherited default.
`config clear <num> --var foo` sends `PATCH /workflow-profile/variables` with `foo` set to JSON null, and against a T-001 server `config get` no longer lists `foo` while other variables remain.
`config clear <num> --prompt greeting` sends `DELETE /workflow-profile/prompts/greeting`; other prompts remain.
`config clear <num> --var foo --prompt greeting` issues both the variables PATCH and the prompt DELETE and leaves everything else intact.
`config clear <num>` with no flags makes no HTTP request, prints a clear message, and exits non-zero.

CLI integration tests assert the emitted method/path/body (including that `--var` produces a JSON null value in the PATCH body) and the no-op path; a test confirms end-to-end removal when run against the T-001 server behavior (or a fake handler asserting the null payload).
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 because `--var` removal only works once the server treats overlay null as key removal; without T-001 the CLI would emit the correct null payload but the key would persist. The CLI itself is correct regardless — the dependency ensures the feature is actually functional.
